text.p: These are the main stories reported in the Angolan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher visited Angola for four hours on Monday to urge forward the implementation of a peace plan between the government and the former rebel UNITA movement.
- Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos told Christopher during his visit that he regarded as a "good sign" the arrival in Luanda of a second group of Unita generals last Friday.
- The International Monetary Fund representative Michel Camdessus began talks with the Angolan government and its economic team on the country's economy.

- U.S. Under Secretary for African Affairs George Moose could not hold talks on Monday with Unita leader Jonas Savimbi due to bad weather in the central highlands from where Savimbi controls his movement.

- The United Nations special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blondin Beye, is due to travel to see Savimbi in Bailundo on Tuesday to brief him on the outcome of a security council meeting which extended the U.N. peacekeeping mandate to Angola by two months.
